edges.description: The c.1630G>T allele activates a cryptic donor and changes exon-13 splicing.
Premature termination triggers transcript degradation for the founding variants; this is not universal across PRKG2 alleles.
Some expressed human mutant constructs produce substantially less cGKII protein. These assays do not distinguish reduced synthesis from accelerated turnover.
Altered proteins fail to support the tested kinase-dependent signaling response; the relative contributions of low abundance and catalytic impairment are not resolved for every allele.
Depletion of a coding transcript can reduce the amount of its protein through reduced available template. This contribution is inferred and does not explain all expression defects.
intermediate_mechanisms: Reduced availability of mRNA for translation

edges.description: Reduced available cGKII contributes to reduced signaling capacity, alongside any intrinsic catalytic defect.

Loss of cGKII permits persistent SOX9 nuclear localization and activity in rat and transfection systems. The molecular intermediary is unresolved; direct SOX9 S181/S64 phosphorylation is dispensable for this effect.
Reduced cGKII removes phosphorylation input to GSK3β Ser9; recombinant-protein assays directly demonstrate that substrate reaction.
In the tested human-variant expression systems, impaired cGKII is associated with failure to induce RAF1 Ser43 phosphorylation. Purified variant-enzyme/substrate kinetics were not measured.

Loss and re-expression experiments establish a contribution of cGKII to hypertrophic differentiation. The graph includes two experimentally supported contributing branches, without claiming that they exhaust its actions.
Persistent SOX9 activity contributes to the differentiation defect, as supported by RNA-interference rescue in rat growth-plate chondrocytes.

Loss of inhibitory Ser9 phosphorylation is proposed to leave GSK3β-dependent β-catenin turnover less restrained. Cell-expression and S9A reporter experiments support this route, but turnover kinetics were not measured.

The GSK3β route contributes to delayed hypertrophy: S9A attenuates cGKII-induced markers in cells and Gsk3b haploinsufficiency partially rescues Prkg2-null mice. It is not the upstream mediator of SOX9 nuclear exclusion.

The authors interpret reduced inhibitory RAF1 phosphorylation as the upstream explanation for failure to restrain the MAPK cascade. The expression experiments do not establish Ser43-specific necessity by a RAF1-site rescue.
Disrupted growth-plate maturation compromises longitudinal endochondral bone growth. This tissue-level bridge is supported by rodent histology and bone-length phenotypes.
intermediate_mechanisms: Disordered growth-plate maturation and cartilage replacement

edges.description: Impaired growth-plate growth explains short-limb stature; applying model findings to the human distribution is a biological inference.
Disrupted endochondral growth contributes to middle/distal limb shortening when this presentation is present; some families lack obvious acromesomelia.
Reduced growth of digital bones can contribute to brachydactyly; neither its frequency nor the exact regional developmental explanation is established by the model experiments.
Human mutant constructs yield reduced protein abundance.
edges.limitations: Overexpression does not measure endogenous patient protein levels or distinguish synthesis from turnover.

nodes.description: Two affected half-siblings in a nine-dog family had disproportionate dwarfism. Detailed radiography and CT of the male showed forelimb deformity, premature distal ulnar physeal closure and impaired endochondral ossification. The splice-donor variant cosegregated with the phenotype and was prioritized against 795 control genomes.

Transient expression compared human WT cGKII with R569*, D761Efs*34 and, in a later study, V470G. Cells were challenged with a cGMP analog and FGF2; immunoblots measured cGKII abundance, RAF1 Ser43 phosphorylation and ERK1/2 activation. The studies used three biological experiments for their signaling comparisons.

The naturally occurring approximately 5-kb deletion creates a frameshift and predicted kinase-domain truncation. Rats grow normally initially, then develop shortened limbs and trunk from about four weeks. Growth plates accumulate postmitotic nonhypertrophic cells; experimental tibial fracture healing is also delayed.

Nonsense-mediated decay was reported for the original nonsense and frameshift alleles. The later p.Ala359Leufs*24 carrier fibroblast sample showed a 92:8 wild-type:mutant RNA ratio, consistent with mutant-transcript depletion; that ratio alone is not a direct kinetic measurement of decay.

nodes.description: Global cGKII deficiency causes dwarfism and a disorganized, elongated growth plate. Growth-plate CNP overexpression fails to rescue the skeletal defect. Later detailed mouse work shows a postmitotic, poorly hypertrophic intermediate layer, with growth-plate expansion most evident at two to four weeks and persistent bone shortening after that expansion subsides.

Male compound-mutant mice show partial recovery of skeletal growth and growth-plate differentiation compared with Prkg2-null mice. Recovery is incomplete and refers to the deficit relative to wild type, not the proportion of normal bone length attained.

Prkg2-null mouse growth plates have reduced phospho-Ser9-GSK3β. Recombinant cGKII phosphorylates this inhibitory site directly. Persistence of GSK3β activity is the mechanistic interpretation; the paper did not directly measure degradation kinetics or all downstream substrates.

nodes.description: cGKII expression alters SOX9 localization and SOX9-dependent collagen readouts. Phosphorylation-deficient SOX9 and forced nuclear-localization constructs distinguish nuclear entry from direct SOX9 phosphorylation. The cell systems and readouts differ and are not pooled as one chondrocyte experiment.

Recombinant kinase assays establish GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation. ATDC5 and primary chondrocyte experiments examine hypertrophic markers; ATDC5 measures cytosolic β-catenin, while HEK293 hosts TCF reporters and Axin co-immunoprecipitation. Constitutively active cGKII and phosphorylation-resistant GSK3β S9A probe pathway function. LiCl is a laboratory perturbation, not an established AMDP therapy.
